snippets.text: If I could go back to the start of Aon 2
in Taiwan, there are a lot of things I
had to do differently. Not because the
game was impossible to figure out, but
because there are so many little things
you only understand after you already
spent hours doing them the wrong way.
These are 10 specific things I wish
someone had told me before I started
playing AON 2. There are almost no
useless items. This is probably one of
the biggest things I wish I understood
early. Don't look at an item and
immediately assume it's garbage just
because you don't know what it's for.
AON 2 has a ridiculous amount of items
that look completely useless when you
first start collecting them, but later
turn out to be materials for another
progression system. For example, the
feathers you pick up while exploring
aren't just random collectibles. They
feed into your monolith progression and
eventually help you progress your
amulet. Then you have materials like
horns, leather, and scales. Those look
like typical MMO crafting trash when you
first see them, but they're actually
tied into Balor's Essence and Radiant
Bal's Essence, which are used for later
progression. And obviously, random gear
isn't necessarily trash either. You can
extract it, use it for different
progression systems, or in some cases,
use it as part of another upgrade. If
you don't know what an item does, check
it first. Because one of the easiest
ways to screw yourself over in AON 2 is
deleting something you thought was
worthless and then discovering 3 weeks
later that you suddenly need a hundred
of them. One thing I would absolutely do
differently is actually finish the main
story instead of treating it as
something you can abandon once you
reached max level. The yellow story
quests are basically the backbone of
your leveling progression. And
completing the story also opens up the
next stages of your character
progression. And finishing the story
path is also tied into getting access to
your early yellow weapon. That weapon is
going to serve you for quite some time
until you eventually drop the better
one. So finish the damn story. When you
are starting your endame progression,
stop trying to build the perfect
character immediately. Your first
priority is getting your gear score high
enough to unlock the next pieces of
content because early on you are
replacing gear constantly. So early
progression should be much more
straightforward. Get gear score, unlock
content, get better gear, repeat. Then
once your gear starts becoming somewhat
you're actually going to keep, that's
when you start worrying much more about
combat power. That's where your mana
stone, soul binding, skills, arcana, pet
genus, and all the other layers start
becoming much more important. Gear score
gets you through the door. Combat power
is how you make your character stronger
once you're there. Most players assume
that ascension quests only happen during
leveling. Well, it keeps going after you
reach level 45. Eventually, by doing
content, you will fill up the fourth
ascension quest gauge, which is the most
important one because you will get the
yellow tier bracelet and legendary
wings, as well as PvP amulet. The
bracelet is the best bracelet you will
be able to equip for quite a while until
you reach Ludra and get the bracelet
drop there. and legendary wings will
make flying and flying combat much more
effective because of the increased
flight power and other attacks. Another
thing I wish I had prioritize sooner,
your belt and amulet are not the normal
gear pieces. They have their own
progression system and their own
enhancement materials. The belt is tied
to strongholds while the amulet is tied
to the feather monolith side of
progression. Both can be pushed into
higher grades through substance morph.
They are permanent parts of your
character progression and getting them
into the yellow tier gives you a really
nice chunk of stats without relying on
some random dungeon drop. So, make sure
you are completing every single
stronghold in your faction map and the
opposite faction map as you will not
have enough materials for upgrading it
to yellow tier without completing the
opposite map strongholds. And also make
sure you collect at least 40 feathers
because that should give you enough
materials to upgrade amulets to yellow
tier. Just keep in mind that there is
PvE and PvP amulet and both needs the
same materials. So if you want both at
yellow tier, you will need to collect
more feathers. Here is one thing I
really wish someone showed me on day
one. When you're gliding, you can use
your movement abilities to maintain
momentum instead of just floating across
the map until your flight power
disappears. First, make sure to set your
keybinds for sprint and flight on keys
that are easily accessible. I'm using
shift for sprint and B for flight. The
general idea is activating flight,
looking slightly up with your camera,
pressing shift to gain fast forward
momentum, and then cancelling the flight
mid dash. This will propel you forward,
and as you are falling down, you are
keeping the forward momentum, but not
wasting flight power, meaning you can
move across bigger distances at much
faster speed. This one will save you
from one of the most annoying parts of
AON 2, your inventory becoming a
disaster. First, set up quick storage by
pressing on this button right here. Once
you've configured your storage properly,
you can quickly dump items into the
storage instead of manually clicking
everything around every time your
inventory fills up. I recommend only to
keep potions, food, and combat scrolls.
The rest you can quick storage. Then
there's also auto extract, which lets
the game automatically handle equipment
extraction instead of forcing you to
manually go through every garbage piece
of gear you've collected. Aon2 added
automatic equipment extractions directly
to the cube system. And trust me, you
want this because once you're regularly
running content, you're going to come
back with a ridiculous amount of
equipment. You don't want to finish a
dungeon and then spend the next two
minutes clicking through 20 pieces of
garbage. Setting gray, green, and blue
items to auto extract, but keeping the
ones that can be used as supply request
is the best setting. Start farming
arcana and pet genus early. This is the
one I would definitely change from the
way that most people approach it. A lot
of players see their progression and
think, I'll worry about Arcana and pets
later when my gear is good. But that's
exactly why you should start them early.
These aren't just temporary gear pieces
you're going to replace. They are
long-term character progression systems.
Arcana gives you additional stats, skill
levels, and set effects, while pedagog
genus inside provides another layer of
permanent progression. And the best part
is that you can build these systems
while doing the rest of your
progression. You are already running
content, you are already killing
monsters. Start building these systems
in the background from the beginning.
You don't have to completely obsess over
them. Just don't leave them untouched
like I did. Flash runes can break. They
are the weird exception to the normal
enhancement system. The rune slot is the
only one that can actually be destroyed
through failed enhancement with the risk
beginning once you're pushing beyond the
early safe levels. So, when you get your
first classroom, don't look at it like a
normal piece of gear and think that you
can max it out. That's not how you want
to approach it. Plus two is where I
would stop early on. Once you start
pushing beyond that, you're no longer
just spending materials, but you're
gambling with the rune itself. Later,
when you have spare runes and you are
intentionally pushing enhancement,
that's a different story. But when
you're starting out, don't throw a
perfectly good rune away because you
wanted one more upgrade plus to it and
then stop. If you're doing not this
style during augo event, there is a
special strategy that has been used for
a long time in Taiwan. You have one
player whose only goal is to collect
every bonus orb that appears, regardless
of where the safe tile is. For the first
six rounds, the other five players only
need to stand in the one safe tile and
then not touch any of the bonus orbs.
Let the player collecting them clear up
safe spots, then go into the safe tile.
At round seven and eight, just stand
outside AFK and don't get into any of
the tiles or touch the bonus orbs. With
a distract player that is collecting
orbs will be rank one while five other
players will all be rank two with 500
points each. Meaning all six players
will get the max rewards as only rank
one and rank two get highest rewards.
Also in general if you are not top two
in any shugo miniame do not use keys to
open the rewards. And also do not do
shugo until you reach level 45 because
you get the rewards also based on your
level. And honestly, that's it when it
comes to the kind of stuff I wish
someone had told me before I started Aon
2. Not another giant spreadsheet telling
you exactly what to farm every hour of
the day. Just the little things that
make the game way easier to understand
from the beginning. Because there are
enough systems in A2 already, you don't
need to learn all of them in the hard
way.
